set.debate.evidence_yes: In a case-crossover study of 3,882 people with a heart attack, the risk of onset in the 60 minutes after cannabis use was 4.8 times baseline; 37 had smoked cannabis within 24 hours and 9 within 1 hour of presentation (Mittleman et al., 2001, as relayed by Page et al., 2020, and Hall & Degenhardt, 2009), and in a follow-up of 1,913 of them mortality over 3.8 years rose with frequency of use, 2.5 times with use less than weekly and 4.2 times with use more than weekly (as relayed by Hall & Degenhardt, 2009, without intervals; the AHA statement says many mortality findings of these smaller follow-up studies did not reach statistical significance). Among 2,097 young adults treated for a heart attack at two academic hospitals, adjusted hazard ratios for all-cause and cardiovascular death were 1.99 and 2.22 among people who used cocaine and marijuana, as the statement's table words it (DeFilippis et al., 2018, as relayed by Page et al., 2020). In a population survey, past-year use went with 3.3 times the rate of stroke or transient ischaemic attack and a rate ratio of 2.3 (1.1 to 4.5) after adjustment that included tobacco, the excess lying in weekly or more frequent use (4.7, 2.1 to 10.7); in a US survey of adults aged 18 to 44 the adjusted OR for stroke was 1.82 (1.08 to 3.10), and 2.45 (1.31 to 4.60) with use on more than 10 days a month (Hemachandra et al., 2016, and Parekh et al., 2020, both as relayed by Page et al., 2020). A health-record database found a 3-year incidence of heart attack of 1.37% against 0.54% (RR 2.53, 2.45 to 2.61), an inpatient database found heart-attack admissions of young adults of 0.23% against 0.14% among people using cannabis without other substances, and a systematic review of studies and case reports found that 28 of 33 studies suggested a higher risk of both acute coronary syndrome and chronic cardiovascular disease (all as relayed by Page et al., 2020). Laboratory studies show dose-related rises in heart rate and angina brought on by smoking cannabis in people with heart disease, exercise time to angina falling by 48% against placebo in one. Hall (2015) reads the evidence as consistent with adverse cardiovascular effects in middle-aged and older adults, adds a French series of cannabis-related hospitalisations that included heart attacks and a fatal stroke in young adults with no other known risk factors, and concludes that cannabis smoking by middle-aged adults probably increases the risk of heart attack; Volkow et al. (2014) describe use as associated with vascular conditions that raise the risk of heart attack, stroke and transient ischaemic attack during intoxication.
